title: Email claiming you won a $500,000 sweepstakes
subject: OFFICIAL NOTICE: Your $500,000 winning check is ready for delivery

segments.text: Congratulations! Your email address was selected in our annual grand prize drawing.
You have won a verified cash award of $500,000 and a new luxury vehicle.

flag.reason: You cannot win a real contest or lottery that you never entered.

segments.text: Federal lottery regulations require an upfront state processing and delivery fee of $450 before we can dispatch the armored courier.

flag.reason: Real lotteries and sweepstakes never ask winners to pay upfront fees or taxes to release prize money.

segments.text: Please send this $450 fee today using store gift cards or money vouchers to our claims agent.

flag.reason: Legitimate organizations never accept prize processing fees or taxes in gift cards or prepaid vouchers.

explanation: Legitimate sweepstakes never require winners to pay fees, taxes, or shipping upfront to collect prize money. If you have to pay money to get a prize, it is an advance-fee scam.
takeaways: You never have to pay money upfront to claim a real prize.
You cannot win a contest you never entered.

title: Donating safely to disaster relief
prompt: Following a severe flood, you want to donate $50 to help affected families. Which donation method is safe?

options.label: Visit an established, accredited charity website that you look up yourself on CharityNavigator.org or give.org
Send $50 through a peer-to-peer payment app to an individual account listed in an emotional social media message
options.note: The poster claims they are buying supplies today

reasons.a: Correct: Independent charity evaluator websites verify that donations go directly to transparent, established relief operations with audited finances.
reasons.b: Risky: After major disasters, scammers set up counterfeit social media appeals to pocket donations. Peer-to-peer mobile transfers to individuals offer zero accountability.

explanation: Scammers exploit natural disasters by creating fake charities and emotional crowdfunding requests. Always look up charities independently through trusted evaluators like Charity Navigator or BBB Wise Giving Alliance.
takeaways: Never send disaster donations to unknown individuals via mobile transfer apps.
